content: Melvin-Koushki describes Shāh Niʿmat Allāh Valī (ca. 730-834/1330-1431) as a prolific Persian writer with seven explicitly lettrist works, who appears to have drawn his lettrism largely from Ibn ʿArabī's Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya; MK calls it “the most complementary of contemporary forms of the science” with respect to Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's project, while stressing that Niʿmat Allāh is a popularizer, not an original thinker.
